title: Verdict
description: The Inspector's return. Passed to codex as --output-schema <path>, which takes the file path; passed to claude as --json-schema <json>, which takes the file CONTENTS inline — the claude adapter reads this file and inlines it, because passing a path fails with "--json-schema is not valid JSON". The Inspector is briefed from the ORIGINAL ORDERS plus the branch, never from the Engineer's account of what it did. Mirrors src/contracts/report.ts — test/contracts.test.ts fails if the two drift. NO `$schema` KEY: claude --json-schema cannot resolve the 2020-12 meta-schema URI and rejects the file outright. STRICT MODE: every property appears in `required` at every level and every optional property is nullable, because codex --output-schema uses OpenAI strict structured outputs, which rejects any property missing from `required`. Both rules are asserted by test/contracts.test.ts.

verdict.description: pass = the branch satisfies the original orders; fail = it does not.

findings.description: At most five. Any blocker means fail.

testsRun.description: Did the Inspector actually execute the suite, or only read? pass with testsRun=false is a distinguishable and suspicious state.

testCommand.description: The exact command run, so a human can reproduce the verdict. null when no tests were run.

behaviours.description: One entry per NUMBERED behaviour in the spec — index-matched, not restated. null when the campaign was run from a free-text objective and there is no spec to account for. When a spec was supplied, every one of its behaviours must appear exactly once here; a behaviour the Inspector could not check is 'not-verified', not an entry left out. A missing number is indistinguishable from a clause nobody looked at, which is the failure this field exists to make impossible.

behaviour.description: 1-based index into the spec's behaviours list. The number is the contract — it lines this entry up with the clause without restating its text, because a restated clause is a paraphrase and a paraphrase is where a clause quietly becomes an easier one.

status.description: met = verified to hold. not-met = verified to be absent or wrong. not-verified = the Inspector could not check this one. not-verified is an honest answer, not a failure — it is strictly better than omitting the entry, because an omission looks identical to a clean bill of health.

note.description: One line: how it was checked, or why it could not be.

file.description: Repo-relative where possible, so it survives the worktree being returned. null when the finding is not about a file.

line.description: 1-based. null when the finding is not about a line.
